Hutatma Rajguru Chowk, Madam Cama Road, Mantralaya Mumbai-32
Dated: 31 July, 2026

Read:

Government Resolution:
The Higher and Technical Education Department, exercising its powers under the relevant provisions of the Maharashtra Public Universities Act, 1956 (Act No.XXII of 1956) and the Maharashtra Engineering Colleges Regulation General Rules, 2016, hereby issues this Government Resolution to regulate the management quota admissions process in private unaided engineering colleges within the State of Maharashtra. This resolution is necessitated by the observed need for greater transparency and standardization in the admission procedures pertaining to the management quota category and is issued under the authority vested in the Director of Technical Education, Maharashtra State.

01. Private unaided engineering colleges shall not admit more than fifteen percent (15%) of the sanctioned intake capacity as per their respective affiliation with the Maharashtra State Board of Technical Education.
02. Prior to admitting any students through the management quota, each college shall obtain prior approval from the Commissioner of Technical Education.  This approval will be contingent upon submission of a detailed admission schedule and proposed selection criteria.
03. The selection process for management quota admissions shall be entirely merit-based and transparent, adhering strictly to the norms and regulations prescribed by the Maharashtra State Board of Technical Education and as modified by this Government Resolution. The criteria shall include marks obtained in qualifying examinations (e.g., JEE Main), reservation policy, and any other relevant factors as determined by the college.

[Schedules]
Schedule 1: Penalty for Violations - Any private unaided engineering college found to be in violation of these provisions, including exceeding the stipulated percentage intake or deviating from the mandated merit-based selection process, shall be subject to penalties as determined and enforced by the Commissioner of Technical Education. Such penalties may include withdrawal of affiliation with the Maharashtra State Board of Technical Education, leading to non-recognition of degrees awarded by the college.
04.  The Director, Maharashtra State Board of Technical Education, shall monitor the implementation of this resolution and conduct periodic inspections of private unaided engineering colleges to ensure compliance.

Note: It should be implemented strictly.

By order and in the name of the Governor of Maharashtra.

[Officer Name]
Under Secretary to Government
